title: Cycle Jamboard scenario runner & role fractionator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Overview:
This ticket captures a prototype playbook and lightweight toolset ("a 'Cycle Jamboard' runner") for running rapid what-if staffing scenarios across an upcoming product cycle.

Problem statement:
- Current cycle planning meetings surface different staffing proposals but lack a concise, reproducible artifact that: (1) encodes role-level fractions (e.g., 0.25 FE, 0.5 Eng infra), (2) simulates resulting scope that must be cut or deferred, and (3) outputs simple trade-off visualizations for PM/Eng/design sign-off.
- As a result we re-run the same conversations each cycle and lose institutional learning about which triage decisions preserved OKRs with minimal marginal cost.

Goals:
- Build a lightweight scenario runner and a shared jamboard template to capture role fractionation, scope buckets, and measurable outcomes.
- Standardize acceptance criteria for soft-freezes and scoped de-scopes that automatically flag high-risk customer areas.
- Deliver a one-page export (CSV + PNG) that teams can attach to planning notes and to Linear issues.

Success metrics (how we'll know it works):
- Reduce cycle planning meeting time related to staffing trade-offs by 30% (baseline: average 90 minutes per initiative).
- Increase number of triage decisions persisted as artifacts by 4x vs last 3 cycles.
- Two pilot teams use the jamboard-runner and report improved clarity in rollforward decisions.

Proposed approach:
1) Designer: produce a Jamboard template that maps roles, FTE fractions, and scope buckets (MVP lanes: Must, Should, Could, Defer).
2) PM: prepare 3 canonical scenarios per initiative (baseline, conservative, aggressive) with estimated story-point burn and critical-path flags.
3) Engineering: provide a minimal scenario runner script that consumes the jamboard CSV export and computes: estimated capacity utilization, expected sprint velocity delta, and a prioritized list of scope items to trim to meet target capacity.
4) Output: one-page summary artifact (PNG + CSV) and a recommended 'soft-freeze trigger' line (e.g., >10% cross-team late-blocked work).

Trade-offs considered:
- Fidelity vs speed: we intentionally keep the model heuristic (no ML) to avoid long setup; prioritization logic is simple (score = criticality / effort).
- Centralization vs autonomy: templates encourage shared language but teams can opt out for the first two pilots.
- Tooling scope: we will not integrate with roadmap tooling (Aha/Jira) in MVP; instead we provide links/attachments and a lightweight CSV format for later ingestion.

Required tasks (MVP):
- Design jamboard template and share in Confluence (Design owner: Elena Park).
- Implement CSV schema and a Python runner script (ENG owner: Jonah Martinez).
- PM-run workshops with two product teams to collect sample scenarios (owner: Aisha Kapoor).
- Create acceptance criteria and an export template for Linear attachments.

Artifacts / Links:
- Jamboard template (drive): https://drive.google.com/example/cycle-jamboard-template
- Confluence PRD draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/cycle-jamboard-prd
- GitHub prototype runner (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-tools/pull/402
- Pilot dashboard spec (not implemented): https://docs.internal/redwood/pilot-dashboard-spec

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat outputs as prescriptive rather than advisory. Mitigation: include explicit 'guidance' header and run two coached pilots.
- Risk: Overfitting to story-point estimates. Mitigation: accept velocity variance and include a max-uncertainty flag in the summary.

Next milestones and timeline:
- 2026-02-19: Jamboard template first draft (Design review complete) — DONE.
- 2026-02-26: Runner script prototype that parses CSV and emits utilization table — IN PROGRESS.
- 2026-03-05: Pilot with Growth team (scenario A/B) — SCHEDULED.
- 2026-03-18: Pilot with Platform team and collect feedback — PLANNED.
- 2026-03-24: Consolidate learnings, update playbook, and decide rollout path — TARGET DUE_DATE.
